Plan samples Before prepping vials, you must consider what range of dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) you expect in your samples. The sensitivity range is determined by the method blank, the water volume, the lower limit of mass for which we can consistently measure carbonate standards (~10 µg), and the detector saturation / linearity effects on the isotope ratio mass spectrometer (IRMS). DBN has optimized procedures to lower blanks, which are reflected in this procedure, although further blank reduction is an ongoing project. Below are some guidelines of appropriate volumes to use: A 1 mL water sample in a 12 mL Exetainer will be good for most freshwater and marine systems (sensitivity range ~ 300 – 4000 µM on Thermo GasBench - Delta V IRMS). If you expect [DIC] > 4000 µM, you can use less sample (i.e. 0.5 ml water). If you expect [DIC] < 300 µM, you can use a larger sample size, i.e. 100 mL blue-butyl stoppered serum vial with a 50 mL water sample. Note, this requires manual sampling with the GasBench needle. If your system has a wide range of [DIC], you can take replicate samples at different water volumes (i.e. for Oman ophiolite, where [DIC] ranges ~3500 - <10 µM, DBN takes 1 mL and 50 mL samples for DIC) Plan method blanks Also, consider what you will use as a method blank. At minimum, you must purge (1-3) vial(s) with helium during sample preparation, and subsequently add decarbonated water + H 3 PO 4. If you plan to have a quick turnaround time between preparing samples and analyzing them (<1 week), and are confident that you will return with samples, you can save time by preparing your full standard suite at the same time as you prepare your samples. If the period between sample preparation and analysis is longer (weeks to months), or if you have any doubt that you will return with samples (due to mishaps in field or new experimental design etc.), you should probably wait to prepare standards until a day before analysis to ensure that your standards are unaltered and to avoid wasting time and standards for a run that never occurs. If the latter applies to you, then prepare a set of blanks as you prepare your samples and another set of blanks the day prior to analysis to check for 1) diffusion between sample preparation and analysis and 2) the repeatability of your blank preparation. Ideally, blanks should be brought into the field because diffusion is a function of pressure gradients and temperature, which may be different in the lab compared to your sampling site. In addition to the He purge + water blank mentioned previously, He-only, He + H 3 PO 4 only, and/or He + carbonate mineral standard + water + H 3 PO 4 can be prepared to test for CO 2 loss/gain, and to determine the sources error, if necessary. The steps below describe the full laboratory procedure for preparing samples and/or standards. Depending on your specific sampling and blank preparation strategy, some steps may not apply. In any case, stop when you reach the centrifugation step, and finish centrifugation and equilibration the day prior to analysis on the IRMS. Exetainer® 12ml Vial - Round Bottom (vial, Labco, 938W x 1000, https://www.labco.co.uk/products/standard-exetainer-cap/product/557-exetainer-12ml-round-bottom/category_pathway-15 ) Wheaton™ Serum Bottles and Vials (vial, DWK Life Sciences, 06-406J, 100 mL nominal volume, https://www.fishersci.com/shop/products/wheaton-serum-bottles-vials-15/06406j#?keyword=06-406J )

steps.title: Measure 100 mL vial volumes (optional)
steps.instruction: Label each 100 mL vial with a unique ID, record the laboratory temperature, cap with a blue butyl stopper, weigh the empty vial, fill it completely with de‑ionized water using a 60 mL syringe and two 23 G needles (ensure no bubbles), re‑weigh, and calculate the water volume from the mass using the density of water (≈0.998 g mL⁻¹ at 20 °C). Perform this for all vials in a single batch to minimise systematic error. Nominally 100 mL vials actually hold a mean of 117 mL (± a few mL).

steps.title: Acid‑wash serum vials overnight
steps.instruction: Place all 100 mL serum vials in an acid bath (e.g., 10 % HCl) and soak overnight to dissolve any carbonate precipitates.

steps.title: Weigh carbonate standards
steps.instruction: Using an XP6 Excellence Plus microbalance (6.1 g capacity, 1 µg readability, Mettler‑Toledo, BZ10134871), weigh the required amount of each carbonate standard, label the corresponding vials, and record the masses.

steps.title: Prepare 85 % phosphoric acid
steps.instruction: Rinse a suitably sized Erlenmeyer flask and a beaker with ultra‑pure water, add two <1 cm stir bars, and carefully transfer 85 % H₃PO₄ into the flask using a glass funnel. Cover both vessels with vented aluminum foil, place on a VWR 220 mini hotplate (room 345, heat 10, stir 1) and heat until bubbling begins; continue heating for 10 min from first bubbles. Turn off heat, allow boiling to stop, then remove from the hotplate. While still hot (1–3 min), draw an aliquot with a 1 mL BD Luer‑Lock syringe. Use safety glasses, lab coat, and nitrile gloves throughout.

steps.title: Prepare ultra‑pure water for standards
steps.instruction: Heat ultra‑pure water (from the GEOM Lab GenPure system) in a beaker on the same hotplate under the same conditions (10 min after bubbling). Transfer the required volume to Exetainer vials using a 3 mL BD Luer‑Lock syringe (or larger syringe for >1 mL). If desired, pass the water through a 0.2 µm PES syringe filter. Keep the syringe tip warm to avoid bubble formation.

steps.title: Inject water into Exetainers
steps.instruction: Fill a 3 mL syringe with the measured water, attach a 0.2 µm polycarbonate inline filter and needle, discard the initial water, refill, remove any bubbles, then inject the water into each Exetainer right‑side‑up. Withdraw the syringe swiftly while holding the needle to prevent loss.

steps.title: Inject phosphoric acid into Exetainers
steps.instruction: Using the hot 85 % H₃PO₄ aliquot, inject acid into each Exetainer at a water : acid ratio of 10 : 1 (e.g., 1 mL water → 100 µL acid). Apply the “nurse” technique (invert and flick) to eliminate bubbles from the syringe. Replace the syringe if the tip deforms; needles may be reused between vials provided the acid is not excessively hot.

steps.title: Clean Exetainer septa
steps.instruction: After all injections, wipe the septum of each Exetainer with a paper towel or Kimwipe to remove any residual liquid.

steps.title: Cap vials with stopper and crimp
steps.instruction: Insert a thick blue chlorobutyl stopper into each vial; autoclave the stopper beforehand to improve pliability if desired. Secure an aluminum crimp top (DWK 20 mm) onto the stopper using a Wheaton crimper. Then gently screw the cap onto the vial until slight resistance is felt, turn an additional ¼ turn, and verify a faint septum indentation through the cap aperture. Replace any puckered caps.

steps.title: Initial helium purge (5 min)
steps.instruction: Attach two 23 G PrecisionGlide hypodermic needles (0.064 cm × 2.5 cm) to the septum, placing the inflow needle slightly deeper than the outflow needle. Connect the outflow needle to a water‑filled tube to visualise bubbles. Purge each vial with Ultra‑Pure Carrier 5.5 % He (Airgas, CGA‑580, catalog #HE UPC300) for 5 minutes, aiming for ~5 bubbles s⁻¹. Use fresh needles for each puncture and keep He partial pressure consistent across vials.

steps.title: First centrifugation
steps.instruction: Place the capped Exetainers upright in a tube rack (12 mL round‑bottom vials fit in 15 mL conical slots) on an Eppendorf 5810R centrifuge. Balance the rotor, then centrifuge at 2500 rpm for 5 minutes. After spinning, visually inspect for carbonate particles on the walls; if present, swirl the liquid to resuspend and repeat centrifugation until the walls are clean.

steps.title: Equilibrate on shaker
steps.instruction: Transfer the vials (caps on) to a tube rack on a New Brunswick C1 platform shaker. Set the speed to ~150 rpm (speed 40 on this model) and shake for 15–18 hours at room temperature, preferably in the stable‑isotope laboratory to match the analysis temperature.

steps.title: Second helium purge (30 min)
steps.instruction: After equilibration, repeat the helium purge using the same needle arrangement, but purge each vial for 30 minutes while maintaining ~5 bubbles s⁻¹. Use new needles for each puncture.

steps.title: Second centrifugation (pre‑analysis)
steps.instruction: Immediately before analysis, centrifuge the vials again at 2500 rpm for 5 minutes to remove condensation that may have formed on the stoppers. Balance the rotor as before.

steps.title: Combust Exetainers in furnace
steps.instruction: Place each Exetainer (cap on) in a muffle furnace, covering the mouth with aluminum foil. Heat to 450 °C and maintain for 5 hours. If vial volumes have been calibrated, imprint the vial ID on the foil with a Sharpie (force imprint; the ink will burn off). After cooling, re‑label the vials as needed. Note: Exetainers have a consistent internal volume of 11.70 ± 0.01 mL, so individual volume measurement is not required for DIC calculations.

steps.title: Load vials into GasBench autosampler
steps.instruction: Place the combusted Exetainers into the GasBench II autosampler according to the instrument’s loading diagram.

steps.title: Prepare GasBench and ConFlo IV
steps.instruction: Ensure the GasBench heat block is turned off (hours to overnight before run). Check the He tank pressure and record it in the Delta notebook. Verify that the ConFlo IV interface displays “CO₂ mode” in the bottom‑left corner.

steps.title: Turn on reference gas and dilutions
steps.instruction: In ConFlo IV > Diagnosis, engage reference‑gas dilutions 1 and 2. Then turn on reference gas (ref II, CO₂) via ConFlo IV Interface > Ref II status. Record the dilution settings in the Delta lab notebook.

steps.title: Run autofocus and record voltage
steps.instruction: Run the autofocus routine (icon shows two blue bars in the upper left). Write down the mass 44 voltage in the Delta lab book and annotate “pass to gas config” next to the value.

steps.title: Turn off reference CO₂ tank
steps.instruction: Close the reference CO₂ tank, wait ~1 minute for the system to flush, then record background voltages for masses 44, 45, and 46 in the Delta notebook.

steps.title: Run CO₂ on/off and linearity sequences
steps.instruction: Open Thermo → Isodat NT → Global → User → ConFlo IV Interface → Sequence and select “20171024 CO2 On Off Lin.seq”. Run both “CO2 On Off.met” and “CO2 Linearity.met”, accepting default prompts. Verify that δ¹⁸O standard deviation ≤ 0.01 ‰ for the on/off test and ≤ 0.15 ‰ for the linearity test.

steps.title: Field sampling – transport He‑purged vials
steps.instruction: Take the He‑purged Exetainers to the field, keeping them upright in a tube rack.

steps.title: Collect water samples in Exetainers
steps.instruction: Fill a 3 mL syringe with field water, attach a 0.2 µm polycarbonate inline filter and needle, discard the initial water, refill, remove bubbles, then inject the sample into an Exetainer right‑side‑up. Withdraw the syringe swiftly while holding the needle. For subsurface pumps, sample directly from the pump stream; otherwise, collect a sub‑sample reservoir (e.g., a 10 L bucket washed three times with site water). Take duplicate or triplicate samples when possible, keep needles and filters sterile, and store samples consistently upright or upside‑down (if upside‑down, perform the centrifugation step during preparation). Bring a tube rack for transport.

steps.title: Troubleshoot needle clogging
steps.instruction: If peak sizes become inconsistent, turn off the sample port and MS capillary (green → gray). Remove the capillary inlet, insert the GasBench needle into an Exetainer filled with >90 % ethanol, and run ethanol through the line for ≥ 10 minutes. Then insert the needle into an air/He‑filled Exetainer and allow ethanol to clear (≈30 minutes or use a heat gun). Re‑install the capillary, replace the graphite ferrule, and trim the capillary tip with a ceramic edge (≈½ turn past finger‑tight).
